newsitem.title: POLAND: ITT-Sheraton sees strong E.Europe growth.
newsitem.headline: ITT-Sheraton sees strong E.Europe growth.

text.p: ITT Sheraton, which on Sunday officially opens its Warsaw hotel, eyes Polish and East European expansion in line with the region's fast economic recovery, the company's European president said on Friday.

"We have the desire to keep pace with the Eastern European development and to be in critical markets as they mature," Robert Cotter said in an interview. ITT Sheraton is a unit of New York-based ITT Corp.

He said the $80 million investment in the construction of Sheraton Warsaw Hotel & Towers, the company's largest single hotel development in Europe, was an example of ITT's commitment to East European growth.
"If you look at East Europe today it's difficult to find a better example than Warsaw of the kind of success that we predict East Europe is going to have," Cotter said.
He said the 350-room hotel, ITT's third Eastern European hotel and 67th in the whole of Europe, has shown high occupancy rates since its unofficial launch in May, signalling a robust local market.

Cotter said the occupancy was about 70 percent in the first two months of operation and after a drop in summer bounced back to 80 percent in September and was expected to hold at this level for the rest of the year.
"Certainly the addition of Sheraton Warsaw has not created any overcapacity..." Cotter said.

He said ITT, which is already managing hotels in Sofia and Zagreb, was also mulling expansion to other East European centres, especially capital cities generally less susceptible to cyclical swings in the hotel business.

"We are looking towards other cities. We are interested in Budapest, in Prague...Belgrade and we are interested in Russia but we don't have anything specific in those cities to talk about," Cotter said.
